Closes the v0.8.13 backwards-compat shim that kept the
refresh token in the JSON body of `/auth/login` and
`/auth/refresh` for one release. v0.8.14+ is cookie-only:
the body field is gone, the body-fallback parse is gone,
and the openapi spec documents the cookie as the only
authoritative channel.

The frontend never read the body field (PR #215 dropped
localStorage and reads from the cookie via
`withCredentials: true`); this PR removes the server-side
emission and the openapi spec's `RefreshRequest` schema,
plus the previously-undocumented `POST /auth/logout`
endpoint that PR #214 added.

## Why

The v0.8.13 release shipped the HttpOnly-cookie storage
for the refresh token (PR #214) and the frontend's
`withCredentials` consumer (PR #215), but kept the body
field as a one-release shim so a pre-v0.8.13 client could
still log in during the upgrade window. v0.8.14 closes
that window: from this release forward, the refresh
token is unreachable from JavaScript (XSS mitigation)
and the only way to send it to the server is the cookie.

The body field was a non-trivial attack surface: even
though the v0.8.13+ frontend ignored it, an XSS payload
in a v0.8.12+ browser could read it from a captured
login response. Removing the field closes that path
unconditionally.

## Changes

- **`backend/internal/auth/handler.go`** — drop the
  `RefreshToken` field from `loginResponse`, drop the
  `refreshRequest` struct, simplify `readRefreshToken`
  to cookie-only. Update all the comments to reflect
  the v0.8.14 state. The 400-on-missing-cookie path
  is now `refresh token cookie is required` (was
  `cookie or body`).
- **`backend/internal/auth/cookie_test.go`** —
  `doLogin` now reads the refresh from the cookie
  (the body field is gone). The body-fallback test
  is inverted to `TestHandleRefresh_BodyIsNotRead`:
  the body-only request now gets 400 + no SET-cookie
  (regression guard against reintroducing a
  body-derived cookie). Drop the now-unused
  `encoding/json` import.
- **`docs/openapi.yaml`** — remove `RefreshRequest`
  schema, remove `refresh_token` from `LoginResponse`
  required+properties, add `Set-Cookie` headers to
  `/auth/login` and `/auth/refresh` 200 responses,
  add the previously-undocumented `POST /auth/logout`
  endpoint with its 204 + clear-cookie contract.
- **`frontend/src/api/services/auth.ts`** — drop the
  `refreshToken` field from the `LoginResponse`
  interface. Update the `logout()` comment to reflect
  v0.8.14 (body-fallback closed).
- **`frontend/src/stores/auth.ts`** — update the
  `login()` body-of-comment about the v0.8.13 shim
  to "closed in v0.8.14".
- **`frontend/src/api/client.ts`** — update the
  response-interceptor comment about `refresh_token`
  (gone in v0.8.14, no longer camelized).
- **`frontend/src/types/api.d.ts`** — regenerated by
  `npm run codegen`. New `/auth/logout` operation
  in the `operations` map; `LoginResponse` no longer
  has `refresh_token`; `RefreshRequest` schema is
  removed.

## Migration notes for operators

v0.8.14 is a **drop-in replacement for v0.8.13** (no
wire-format change for a v0.8.13 frontend). The
sequence is the same "server before client" rolling
upgrade as the v0.8.13 cut:

1. Upgrade the panel image to v0.8.14 first.
   The v0.8.13 frontend continues to work
   unchanged (it doesn't read the body field).
2. Upgrade the UI image to v0.8.14+ to drop
   the `refreshToken` type from the generated
   `LoginResponse`. A v0.8.14 frontend + v0.8.13
   panel is broken (panel sets the cookie, but
   v0.8.13 frontend would not refresh on 401
   because it still expects the body).

After the rolling upgrade, the wire format is
unambiguous: `POST /auth/login` and `POST
/auth/refresh` responses carry only the access
token in the body, the refresh token is in the
`Set-Cookie: aegis_rt=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict;
Path=/; Max-Age=2592000; Secure` header.
